terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, with the dative, or nē or ut
evidence: Cic. Att. 11.3.3: cūrā et prōvidē nē quid eī dēsit
terms.comment: Of seeing to it in advance that someone has what they need.

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.12: quōs cārōs habeat tuērīque dēbeat
terms.comment: Classically to look at, and above all to look after, maintain and protect (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Ter. Ad. 481–482: sōlus omnem familiam sustentat
terms.comment: Of keeping a household. In composed Latin, “his family” is suī or domus: familia is the whole household.
Of feeding and keeping people or animals.

phrases.latin: studeat parāre ea, quae suppeditent ad cultum et ad victum, nec sibi sōlī, sed conjugī, līberīs cēterīsque, quōs cārōs habeat tuērīque dēbeat
phrases.english: he strives to get what will provide clothing and food, not for himself alone but for his wife, his children and the others he holds dear and is bound to look after

phrases.latin: omnibus rēbus cūrā et prōvidē nē quid eī dēsit
phrases.english: take every care and see to it that she lacks nothing

phrases.latin: Neque iners, alit illās: sōlus omnem familiam sustentat
phrases.english: and he’s no idler: he keeps them; he alone supports the whole household

sources: Lewis & Short: provideo · Lewis & Short: tueor · Lewis & Short: sustento · Lewis & Short: alo
